title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Average Aus Salary with a 38-Hour Week
description: Convert hourly rates to annual pay using a 38-hour week and 52 weeks. Learn about the National Minimum Wage, casual loading, super, and how the average aus salary compares.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours a week, the annual gross salary is the hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52). The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, giving $52,254.80 a year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 (weeks per year). For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. This calculation assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the base rate for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and occupations, found in pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman. Most employees are covered by an award, so their minimum pay is likely above the National Minimum Wage. Always check the relevant award for your correct rate.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay and annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When converting to annual salary, use the casual hourly rate in the formula. Remember that casual hours can vary, so your actual annual income may differ. Superannuation is paid on top of the casual rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Your Hourly Rate and the 38-Hour Year

When you’re offered an hourly rate or a salary, the first step is to see how they compare. The standard full-time working week in Australia is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. To find your annual gross salary, multiply your hourly rate by 38, then by 52 weeks. This gives you a clear picture of your **average aus salary** before tax and super.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour:
- Weekly: $30 × 38 = $1,140
- Fortnightly: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280
- Annual: $1,140 × 52 = $59,280

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a useful benchmark, but your actual pay may vary.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most workers, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry and role. You can find the correct rate for your job using [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Award rates often include classifications based on skill level and experience. For example, a hospitality employee may have a higher minimum than the National Minimum Wage. Always check your award to ensure you’re being paid correctly.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate because they don’t get paid sick leave or annual leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When calculating your annual salary as a casual, use this loaded rate in the formula. Remember, casual hours can fluctuate, so your actual income may differ from the estimate.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, super adds about $6,270.58 per year (12% of $52,254.80). Super is not part of your salary; it’s an extra contribution to your retirement fund.

### The Average Aus Salary: How Do You Compare?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, which equates to an annual salary of about $108,352.40 (before tax). This figure is often cited as the **average aus salary** for full-time workers. However, when all employees (including part-time) are included, total earnings average $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118.40 per year.

These averages can help you see where your pay sits. If your hourly rate is above $26.44, you’re above the minimum. The average full-time hourly rate (based on $2,083.70 for 38 hours) is about $54.83 per hour. But remember, averages can be skewed by high earners. Your own rate depends on your industry, experience, and award.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,254.80), the tax would be approximately:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $7,254.80 ($45,001 to $52,254.80) = $2,176.44
- Total tax: $6,196.44
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,045.10
- Total deductions: $7,241.54
- Take-home pay: about $45,013.26 per year, or $865.64 per week.

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate. Remember, this doesn’t include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – use the checkbox instead. The timesheet assumes a 38-hour week, but you can adjust hours if needed.

For more detailed comparisons, see our [reference tables](/data) for award rates and historical minimum wages. You can also explore [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for different work patterns.

### Key Points to Remember

- Annual gross salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For full-time, use 38 hours.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour; casual rate is $33.05.
- Award rates are often higher – check your pay guide.
- Super is 12% paid on top, up to the contribution base.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay.
- The average aus salary for full-time workers is around $108,350 per year, but your actual pay depends on your job.

Understanding these basics helps you negotiate offers, plan your budget, and ensure you’re paid fairly. For more guidance, visit the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) or use our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.
